steps: Read the question — what quantity are you finding? (energy, power, speed, height?)
Recall the correct equation from memory
Convert all units (g→kg, mins→s, km/h→m/s, kJ→J)
State your answer with the correct unit (J, W, kJ, kW)
method_card.title: Energy: KE, GPE and Power
method_card.content:
This lesson covers five recall equations — none of them are on the equation sheet, so you need to know them from memory.

Approach for every calculation:

  1. Read the question — what are you asked to find?
  2. Identify the correct equation from memory
  3. List the values you're given and convert units if needed
  4. Substitute into the equation and calculate
  5. Write your answer with the correct unit

Common pitfalls:

  • Speed is squared in the KE equation — doubling speed quadruples KE
  • Convert time to seconds before using the power equation
  • Convert mass to kg (not grams) and speed to m/s
  • Use \(g = 9.8\) N/kg unless told otherwise
  • 1 kJ = 1000 J, 1 kW = 1000 W, 1 MW = 1,000,000 W

exam_context.frequency: Every exam — energy calculations appear on every Paper 1

gold.display: A skydiver of mass 75 kg falls from 4000 m to 3000 m. Calculate the speed they would reach if all the lost GPE converted to KE. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Use the height difference (4000 − 3000 = 1000 m), not the total height.

gold.display: A car of mass 1100 kg travels at 20 m/s. The driver brakes, and the car decelerates to 8 m/s. Calculate the work done by the brakes.
An electric motor has a power rating of 2.5 kW. It lifts a 80 kg object 6 m in 4 seconds. Calculate the efficiency of the motor. Give your answer as a percentage. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: Useful output = mgh = 80 × 9.8 × 6 = 4704 J. Total input = Pt = 2500 × 4 = 10,000 J. Efficiency = 4704/10,000 × 100 = 47.04%.
Convert kW to W: 2.5 kW = 2500 W. Then total input energy = 2500 × 4 = 10,000 J.

gold.display: Two students climb the same flight of stairs (height 4 m). Student A has mass 50 kg and takes 5 seconds. Student B has mass 70 kg and takes 8 seconds. Which student has greater power output? Enter A or B.

misconceptions.message: Power A = mgh/t = (50 × 9.8 × 4)/5 = 392 W. Power B = (70 × 9.8 × 4)/8 = 343 W. Student A has greater power.

gold.display: A ball of mass 0.3 kg is dropped from a height of 10 m. It bounces back to a height of 6 m. Calculate the energy dissipated during the bounce. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: GPE before = 0.3 × 9.8 × 10 = 29.4 J. GPE after = 0.3 × 9.8 × 6 = 17.64 J. Energy dissipated = 29.4 − 17.64 = 11.76 J.

gold.display: A wind turbine generates 1.5 MW of power. How much energy does it transfer in one day? Give your answer in standard form.

bronze.display: A car has a mass of 1200 kg and travels at 15 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.

misconceptions.message: Square the speed first: 15² = 225. Then KE = ½ × 1200 × 225 = 135,000 J.
Don't forget the ½. KE = ½ × 1200 × 225 = 135,000 J, not 270,000 J.

bronze.display: A 0.5 kg ball is held 4 m above the ground. Calculate its gravitational potential energy. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A force of 50 N pushes a box 8 m along the floor. Calculate the work done.

misconceptions.message: Work done = force × distance = 50 × 8 = 400 J.

bronze.display: A kettle transfers 180,000 J of energy in 3 minutes. Calculate its power in watts.

misconceptions.message: Convert minutes to seconds first: 3 min = 180 s. P = 180,000 ÷ 180 = 1000 W.

bronze.display: A runner of mass 60 kg sprints at 8 m/s. Calculate their kinetic energy.

misconceptions.message: Square the speed: 8² = 64. KE = ½ × 60 × 64 = 1920 J.

bronze.display: A bag of mass 3 kg is lifted onto a shelf 2.5 m high. Calculate the GPE gained. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A motor does 5000 J of work in 20 seconds. Calculate its power.

misconceptions.message: Power = energy ÷ time = 5000 ÷ 20 = 250 W. Don't multiply.

bronze.display: Which equation would you use to calculate the energy stored by an object lifted above the ground?

misconceptions.message: An object above the ground has gravitational PE. Use Eₚ = mgh. KE is for moving objects.

silver.display: A cyclist and bike have a combined mass of 80 kg and travel at 12 m/s. Calculate the kinetic energy in kJ.

misconceptions.message: Square the speed first: 12² = 144. Then ½ × 80 × 144 = 5760 J = 5.76 kJ.

silver.display: A 60 W light bulb is left on for 2 hours. Calculate the energy transferred in kJ.

misconceptions.message: Convert hours to seconds: 2 h = 7200 s. E = Pt = 60 × 7200 = 432,000 J = 432 kJ.

silver.display: A crane lifts a 400 kg load to a height of 15 m. Calculate the work done by the crane. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

misconceptions.message: First find the weight: W = mg = 400 × 9.8 = 3920 N. Then work done = Fs = 3920 × 15 = 58,800 J.

silver.display: A car of mass 900 kg accelerates from rest to 30 m/s. Calculate the work done on the car.

misconceptions.message: Work done = change in KE = ½ × 900 × 30² = ½ × 900 × 900 = 405,000 J.
Don't forget to square the speed: 30² = 900. KE = ½ × 900 × 900 = 405,000 J.

silver.display: A 1500 W motor lifts a 50 kg mass. How high can it lift the mass in 10 seconds? Give your answer to 1 d.p. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
A 200 g tennis ball is served at 50 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.

misconceptions.message: Convert grams to kg: 200 g = 0.2 kg. KE = ½ × 0.2 × 50² = ½ × 0.2 × 2500 = 250 J.

worked_examples.question: A ball of mass 0.4 kg is thrown at a speed of 10 m/s. Calculate its kinetic energy.
A crane lifts a 250 kg beam to a height of 12 m in 30 seconds. Calculate the power of the crane. (g = 9.8 N/kg)

worked_examples.question: A roller coaster car of mass 500 kg is at the top of a 40 m hill. Calculate its speed at the bottom, assuming all GPE converts to KE. (g = 9.8 N/kg)
